npcRoster.name: Ronna Shaw
npcRoster.publicDescription:
Ronna Shaw is a gruff, battle-seasoned Dwarf quartermaster who has seen too many bright causes ruined by fools with titles and no spine. As a Marduthor-shaped Dwarf, she respects craft, fortification, artillery, logistics, and practical defense far more than speeches, and she will not follow anyone until they prove they can protect people when the walls shake.
At the Aelgrove Guild Desk, Ronna maintains the Freeblade Veil’ heavy stores: thundercoil muskets, siege charges, artillery plans, signal flares, defensive emplacements, and the old guns nobody younger than her knows how to wake properly. She is sharp-tongued, loyal once earned, unimpressed by rank, and deeply hostile toward any faction that hoards weapons or engineering knowledge while settlements are left to die without proper defenses.
npcRoster.settlementAncestryTexture: Aelgrove is a City in Eldermere, under Cooperative Commonwealth, with elevated danger, Beach and grass with water, Deep forest, Partial forest terrain, and public routes by Caravan, Train, Ferry, Steamship. Local records favor Altruistic, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Wood Elf, Elf — Eladrin, Fey-Folk — Faerie. Dwarf reads through the Dwarf entry of the race compendium, within Dwarven and Gnomish Kin, marked by Marduthor. Dwarves are stout, resilient folk deeply tied to stone, craft, and ancestral tradition. They value honor, craftsmanship, and enduring legacies over fleeting trends. Table cues: Darkvision, Dwarven Resilience, Dwarven Toughness, Stonecunning; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Cooperative - Honorable.
publicRumors: Ronna Shaw knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Enkirday.
Ronna Shaw has a contact in Leammipa who will deny everything.

npcRoster.publicDescription: Sturge Gearhand is a Vedalken machinist with a calm voice, clever hands, and the rare gift of making broken people trust broken machines again. He builds pumps, beds, generators, barricades, and improvised defenses for the Freeblade Veil, treating every safe wall and warm lamp as proof that survival can become a home. npcRoster.name: Caetha Redglass
npcRoster.publicDescription:
Caetha Redglass is furious, sharp-tongued, hard to comfort, and even harder to fool, but her cruelty is mostly scar tissue from a life where every offer of kindness came with a hook in it. As a Half-Orc, she carries Nebyrr’s mixed-heritage pull toward survival, structure, and principled endurance, twisted by betrayal into a belief that deals are safer than love and violence is more honest than sympathy.
At the Red Pit Bathhouse, Caetha fights because pain is familiar, coin is clean, and the crowd’s roar is easier to trust than quiet concern. Her long-term addiction is to battle-grade ichor—especially the black-market, rage-bright kind used by pit crews and desperate duelists—and the Brass Concordat sees her as both a dangerous asset and a living witness to how Eldermere’s polished civic order still profits from broken people.

Humans are highly adaptable and found in nearly every environment across the world. They are known for their cultural diversity, short generational cycles, and unmatched versatility among mortal races. globalNamedWeatherDefinitions.What it means: When both moons favor the sea at once, harbor stones vanish and reef roads drown.
A low, quiet tide that exposes mud gates, wreck bones, and hidden causeways.
A low-pressure sea storm arriving with a strong moon tide.
A sudden retreat of water before trench-fed surge returns.
A black-green wall of rain that crosses whole coasts.
Short, sharp squalls that arrive in pairs or trios every few days.
Moonlit fog so bright it makes ships look closer than they are.
A towering thunderhead that forms over heated highlands.
Greenish swamp fog carrying spores, firefly light, and bad directions.
A suffocating, windless heat that freezes sails and tempers alike.
A rotating storm whose calm center is ringed by clear, staring sky.
Low rolling thunder that repeats long before the rain reaches a settlement.
Warm gas-fog from marsh canals and low cave mouths.
A fine crosswind rain that seems to fall sideways from many directions.
Shimmering heat that turns distance into false water and false stone.
Three winds meeting over cliffs, reefs, or a canyon mouth.
A steep, dark swell pushed by far-off pressure changes.
Warm rain that wakes rot, swollen roots, and hungry fungus.
A sudden evening wind that turns forest travel loud and blind.
A hooked dust plume ahead of dryline storms.
Highland lightning that walks along exposed ridges.
Rain-soaked clay roads that swallow carts and boots.
A season when road puddles hide sinkholes, leeches, and false bottoms.
A dry graveyard wind that carries dust, spores, and old sickness.
A clean mountain lift used by skyships and great birds.
A fast pull beneath reef water during strong tide shifts.
Thin cold rain that whistles through ruins and empty rigging.
One storm-fed river splits into several dangerous surges.
A spiraling river or sea current that turns boats sideways.
A soft glowing insect and spore bloom after warm moon rain.

majorWaters.Where it belongs: The eastern deep ocean beyond the horned lands and high islands.

majorWaters.Name: Horundar Storm Ocean
